facts.text: USGS: two companies near Spruce Pine, NC produce US high-purity quartz; the US is estimated world leader in HPQ production.
facts.note: Corrected: USGS gives no global share; 'most of the world's supply' not in official data. BloombergNEF (via Bloomberg/AP 2024) put Sibelco + Quartz Corp at >80% of commercial HPQ; that secondary figure was not opened directly.

facts.text: USGS: no economic substitutes exist for high-purity quartz in most applications; Spruce Pine HPQ exceeds 99.999% purity.
facts.note: USGS also notes China announced 35 Mt HPQ reserves (Apr 2025) testing at 99.995–99.998%.

facts.text: High-purity quartz is made into fused quartz crucibles used to grow silicon ingots that are sliced into semiconductor and solar wafers.
facts.note: USGS does not name the Czochralski process explicitly; the Sumco patent below does.

facts.text: Quartz crucibles used in Czochralski silicon pulling erode and deform at over 1,400°C, limiting their life; they are a consumable.
facts.note: Nuance: crucibles may yield several ingots ('multi-pulling') before discard; 'single-use' is an overstatement.

facts.text: Japan's Shin-Etsu Chemical and SUMCO together account for roughly half of the global silicon wafer market.
facts.note: Corrected from 'majority': DigiTimes says ~50%. A 2026 Nikkei survey (via 36Kr, not opened) reportedly puts the pair at 44.1%.

facts.text: ASML (Netherlands) is the only maker of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment used for the most advanced AI chips.
facts.source_name: Reuters (via The Star), Max A. Cherney
facts.note: Chinese and US efforts to develop alternatives reported; recheck.

facts.text: Ukraine's Ingas (Mariupol) and Cryoin (Odesa) supplied an estimated 45–54% of the world's semiconductor-grade neon before 2022.
facts.note: Reuters calculation from company figures and Techcet data.

facts.text: Japanese firms such as JSR and Tokyo Ohka Kogyo hold about 90% of the global photoresist market, per the US trade agency.
facts.source_name: US International Trade Administration – Japan Country Commercial Guide: Semiconductors
facts.note: Same page also cites Brookings (Jun 2024) at 50% for photoresists overall; ~90% fits advanced/EUV resists. Sumitomo Chemical is a supplier but no share found. Original wording named JSR/TOK/Shin-Etsu/Sumitomo.

facts.text: By some estimates, TSMC produces over 90% of the world's most advanced chips.
facts.note: An estimate, not an audited figure; keep 'by some estimates'.

facts.text: SK hynix (50%) and Samsung (33%) held most HBM market share in Q2 2026; US-based Micron held 18%.
facts.source_name: Counterpoint Research – Global DRAM and HBM Market Share
facts.note: Qualified: Korean firms dominate but Micron is a significant third supplier. SK hynix was 64% in Q2 2025; quarterly tracker, figures change.

facts.text: TSMC's chairman said in 2023 the AI chip shortage stemmed from CoWoS packaging capacity, meeting only about 80% of demand.
facts.source_name: The Register (relaying Nikkei Asia interview with Mark Liu)
facts.note: Primary interview is Nikkei Asia (paywalled, not opened). 2026 DigiTimes reports advanced packaging still tight.

facts.text: USGS: China accounted for 99% of world primary low-purity gallium production.
facts.note: Corrected from 98% to 99% (USGS MCS 2025 and 2026).

facts.text: USGS: China remained the leading global producer and exporter of germanium metal in 2025; global data are limited.
facts.note: Corrected: USGS gives no percentage share for germanium, so 'majority' is not confirmed by USGS.

facts.text: USGS estimates Congo (Kinshasa) mined about 1,300 t of tantalum in 2025, roughly half the world total; Rwanda ranked second (400 t).
facts.note: World total ~2,500 t; Nigeria (390 t) close behind Rwanda. UN experts report M23 coltan is smuggled into Rwanda and mixed with Rwandan output.

facts.text: Dodd-Frank Section 1502 conflict minerals rules cover tantalum, tin, gold and tungsten (3TG).
facts.source_name: US SEC – Conflict Minerals fact sheet

facts.text: EU Conflict Minerals Regulation (EU) 2017/821 covers tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold; importer duties apply from 1 January 2021.
China accounts for about 94% of global sintered NdFeB permanent magnet production.
facts.source_name: Columbia University Center on Global Energy Policy
facts.note: Consistent with IEA rare earths report (94% in 2024) and CSIS (~93%), which blocked direct fetch.

facts.text: Global Witness: Myanmar is the largest source of heavy rare earths; Kachin mining sites are controlled by military-aligned militias.
facts.source_name: Global Witness – Fuelling the future, poisoning the present
facts.note: Report covers Kachin Special Region 1 (militias aligned with the junta); the KIA-held Mai Ja Yang area is also a mining centre. Sites rose >40% from 2021 to 2023. Control has shifted with the conflict.

facts.text: US data centers used about 4.4% of US electricity in 2023; LBNL projects 6.7–12% by 2028.
facts.source_name: US Department of Energy (LBNL 2024 Data Center Energy Usage Report)
facts.note: 176 TWh in 2023; 325–580 TWh projected for 2028 (scenario range).

facts.text: IEA: China's Xinjiang province accounts for 40% of global polysilicon manufacturing.
facts.source_name: Utility Dive (quoting IEA Special Report on Solar PV Global Supply Chains)
facts.note: 2022 data; share has likely shifted. IEA page blocked direct fetch: https://www.iea.org/reports/solar-pv-global-supply-chains/executive-summary

facts.text: Under UFLPA, CBP presumes goods made wholly or partly in Xinjiang are made with forced labour and barred, unless rebutted.
facts.source_name: US Customs and Border Protection – UFLPA

facts.text: Sibelco and The Quartz Corp halted Spruce Pine operations from 26 Sept 2024 after Hurricane Helene; Sibelco restarted about two weeks later.
facts.note: Confirmed by main thread via AP (ABC News) and Bloomberg (2024-10-01/02) coverage; restart: AP 'North Carolina maker of high-purity quartz back operating post-Helene'.

facts.text: China imposed gallium export licensing in Aug 2023, banned exports to the US in Dec 2024, and lifted that ban for one year in Nov 2025.
facts.source_name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 – Gallium / Germanium
facts.note: Germanium chapter confirms the same Aug 2023 licensing and Dec 2024 US ban.

facts.text: China suspended its gallium, germanium and antimony export ban to the US from 9 Nov 2025 until 27 Nov 2026; licensing still applies.
facts.note: URGENT: suspension expires 27 Nov 2026, four days after retrieval. No extension notice found as of 23 Nov 2026. The licensing point comes from Reuters-based coverage (Engineering News, Mining Weekly), not the CNBC page.

facts.text: PLA's 'Strait Thunder-2025A' drills (1–2 Apr 2025) rehearsed blockade and strikes on Taiwan's ports and energy facilities.
facts.note: Widely reported, but the USNI page was blocked (403); confirmed only from multiple search excerpts. Follows Joint Sword-2024A/B.

facts.text: China's 'Justice Mission 2025' drills (29–30 Dec 2025) simulated a blockade of Taiwan and its main ports, Keelung and Kaohsiung.
facts.note: Most recent large-scale drill found. Described as the sixth large-scale war game since 2022.

facts.text: UFLPA's rebuttable presumption took effect 21 June 2022, barring Xinjiang-linked goods unless importers rebut it.
facts.source_name: US Customs and Border Protection – UFLPA

facts.text: CBP told Reuters it had detained 1,053 solar equipment shipments under UFLPA from 21 June to 25 Oct 2022.
facts.note: Reuters wording was 'seized'; CBP said none had yet been released.

facts.text: UN experts reported M23 seized Rubaya in April 2024 and collected at least $800,000 a month from coltan levies.
facts.source_name: Reuters (Sonia Rolley, Alessandra Prentice), via Kitco
facts.note: UN Group of Experts also reported at least 150 t of coltan fraudulently exported to Rwanda in 2024. Rwanda denies backing M23. Mongabay gives Feb 2025 as the control date; Reuters and Al Jazeera say 2024.

facts.text: A landslide at Rubaya coltan mines (28 Jan 2026) killed over 200, per rebel-appointed officials; Rubaya produces ~15% of world coltan.
facts.note: Toll is from M23-appointed officials; AP also reported at least 200 dead. Jan 28 date from Mongabay.

facts.text: A second Rubaya landslide on 3 Mar 2026 killed over 200, per DRC's mines minister; M23 disputed the toll.
facts.note: Published date approximate (March 2026). AP reported an M23 official saying 5 died and blamed 'bombings'.

facts.text: From 1 Sep 2023, Dutch rules required export licences for ASML's TWINSCAN NXT:2000i and later immersion DUV systems.
facts.note: Consistent across ASML, TechPowerUp and The Register (which confirms the NXT:2000i licence requirement), but the ASML page itself was not opened (redirect/403).

facts.text: From 7 Sep 2024, the Netherlands also required Dutch licences for ASML NXT:1970i and 1980i DUV systems; EUV sales already needed licences.
facts.note: Reuters (Toby Sterling, 7 Sep 2024) also reports it.

facts.text: Reports say the Dutch government has never allowed ASML to ship EUV machines to China, after US pressure from 2019–2020.
facts.note: Widely reported but not opened directly; the Reuters original was blocked. Phrase as 'reported'.

facts.text: After Russia's 2022 invasion, Ingas (Mariupol) and Cryoin (Odesa) halted neon production; Cryoin stopped on 24 Feb 2022.
facts.note: Cryoin reported high-purity neon prices up to 500% since December 2021.

facts.text: The 16 Mar 2022 Fukushima-offshore earthquake halted production at Renesas' Naka, Takasaki and Yonezawa chip plants.
facts.note: Naka was back to full wafer-input capacity on 26 Mar 2022 (Renesas update 4). Shin-Etsu wafer-plant impact is only lightly sourced (TrendForce), so it was not used.

facts.text: DRC suspended cobalt exports on 22 Feb 2025, then replaced the ban with quotas from 16 Oct 2025: 96,600 t a year for 2026–27.
facts.source_name: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence / IEA policy database (search excerpts); Africanews
facts.note: Africanews (opened) confirms the Feb 2025 suspension and that exports resumed 19 Dec 2025. Quota dates and figures come from search excerpts (Benchmark, Reuters/mining.com, IEA); those pages blocked fetch. In 2026 ARECOMS clawed back unused H1 quotas.

facts.text: DRC banned trade in minerals from 38 artisanal sites in North and South Kivu, including tantalum ore, extending it six months in Nov 2025.
facts.note: The DRC measure on tantalum is site-level, not a national coltan quota. A Semafor item (23 Sep 2025) on a 'coltan export ban' appears to conflate it with cobalt and is unverified. Masisi/Kalehe detail from Reuters syndication excerpts.

facts.text: Chip-equipment supplier MKS Instruments disclosed a ransomware event on 3 Feb 2023 and suspended operations at some facilities.
facts.note: MKS later estimated a Q1 revenue hit of at least $200M. Applied Materials guided a $250M hit from a supplier's cyber event, linked to MKS by Bloomberg. MKS supplies subsystems, not materials.

facts.text: Simchi-Levi, Schmidt & Wei (HBR, Jan–Feb 2014) measure risk by each node's time to recover (TTR), not by disruption probability.
facts.note: Corrected: the HBR article is from 2014, not 2015. TTR and the Risk Exposure Index are confirmed via MIT News (2014). Time-to-survive is not confirmed in the HBR piece; see simchi_levi_tts.

facts.text: Simchi-Levi et al. (Interfaces, 2015) define time-to-survive as the longest a firm can last without losing demand after a disruption.
facts.note: Exact wording from Appendix B: 'longest time that the firm can last without losing demand after a disruption happens.' Applied at Ford.
